magpylib-studio.pythonPath.description: Python interpreter used to run the magpylib-studio engine. Empty = auto-detect (.venv next to the workspace, then python3).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_listObjects
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the objects in the current Magpylib Studio scene, depth-first. Returns an array of {id, type, label, parent}; 'parent' is the id of the containing Collection (type 'Collection' groups other objects) or null at scene root. The Studio engine starts automatically - never ask the user whether it is running or what the object ids are; call this tool to find out (an empty array just means the scene is empty).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getSchema
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the JSON Schema describing every editable style property of one magpylib scene object (valid dotted paths, types, allowed values). Use it to find the correct path/value before calling the apply edit tool.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_addObject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add ONE new object to the Magpylib Studio scene; to create several objects use the batch tool in a single call instead. 'type' is a dotted magpylib class path like 'magnet.Cuboid', 'magnet.Cylinder', 'magnet.Sphere', 'current.Circle' or 'Sensor'. 'params' are the constructor kwargs (e.g. polarization, dimension/diameter, position; a Sensor position may be a list of [x,y,z] points forming a path). 'rotations' optionally rotates the object after construction (e.g. Halbach arrangements: orbit with anchor 0, then spin in place). Type 'Collection' creates a group; pass 'parent' (a Collection id) to nest an object inside a group - rotations on a Collection rotate the whole group. On failure the result contains the constructor/validation error - fix and retry. Note: on magnets the default magnetization coloring masks the base 'color' style - for a visible solid color also include 'magnetization.mode': 'arrow'.

object_id.description: New unique id for the object (used as the variable name in generated scripts).

style.description: Optional style, dotted paths to values, e.g. {"label": "Ball", "color": "green"}.

parent.description: Optional id of a Collection to nest this object inside; omit for scene root.

rotations.description: Optional rotations applied in order after construction. Each: {"angle": degrees, "axis": "x"|"y"|"z", "anchor": 0 or [x,y,z]}; omit 'anchor' to spin in place, anchor 0 orbits the origin.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_removeObject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove one object from the Magpylib Studio scene by id. To empty the whole scene use the clear scene tool; to remove several (but not all) objects use the batch tool - never chain single removals.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object to remove, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setParam
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set a constructor parameter of a magpylib scene object - position, dimension, diameter, polarization, ... Use this to move or resize objects (style edits use the apply edit tool instead). On failure the result contains the error - fix and retry.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getField
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compute the total magnetic field of all sources in the Magpylib Studio scene, in SI units (B in tesla, H in A/m, coordinates in meters). With no input it evaluates along the scene's sensor path; pass 'points' [[x,y,z], ...] to evaluate at specific locations instead. Returns {field, unit, points, values ([Bx,By,Bz] per point), magnitude}. Use this for quantitative questions ('what is B at the center?') and to MEASURE the effect of scene edits - after editing, call it again and compare.

sensor_id.description: Optional Sensor id to evaluate along; defaults to the first sensor in the scene.

points.description: Optional explicit observer points in meters, e.g. [[0,0,0],[0,0,0.5]]; overrides sensor_id.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_undo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Undo the most recent scene change(s) - style edits, adds, removes, moves, loads; a whole batch is one step. Use when the user asks to undo/revert, or to roll back your own edit that had an unwanted effect. Returns {ok, error?}.

steps.description: How many history steps to undo (default 1).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_rotate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Rotate a scene object by 'angle' degrees about 'axis'. Pass anchor 0 (or [x,y,z]) to ORBIT that point instead of spinning in place - Halbach-style arrangements orbit and spin by the same angle. A list of angles creates an animation path (use start: -1 to append to the existing path). Works on Collections too, rotating the whole group. Prefer the batch tool for many objects.

angle.description: Degrees; a list of degrees creates a path.

anchor.description: Orbit this point: 0 for the origin, or [x,y,z]. Omit to spin in place.

start.description: Path index to apply from; -1 appends to the current path.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_move
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Move a scene object by a RELATIVE displacement [dx,dy,dz] in meters. A list of displacements creates an animation path (use start: -1 to append). To set an absolute position instead, use the set position tool. Works on Collections, moving the whole group.

start.description: Path index to apply from; -1 appends to the current path.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setTransform
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set an object's ABSOLUTE position and/or orientation in world coordinates (meters, degrees). 'position' is [x,y,z] or a path [[x,y,z],...]; 'orientation' is a rotation vector [rx,ry,rz] in degrees. Use the move/rotate tools for relative changes.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_clearScene
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove ALL objects from the Magpylib Studio scene in one call. Always use this instead of removing objects one by one when the user wants to clear/clean/empty the scene.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_batch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Apply several Magpylib Studio scene operations in ONE call - always prefer this over chaining single tool calls when creating, editing, or removing multiple objects (e.g. building an array of magnets). Operations run in order; failures don't stop the rest. The result lists per-operation outcomes ({ok, error?}) - fix failed ones and retry only those. Batchable methods: add_object, remove_object, move_object (reparent into/out of Collections: {object_id, parent?}), apply_edit, set_param, move, rotate, set_transform, clear_path, reset_style, clear_scene (their params match the corresponding single tools).

params.description: Arguments for the method, same shape as the corresponding single tool (e.g. {"object_id": "m1", "type": "magnet.Cuboid", "params": {...}} for add_object).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_applyEdit
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set one style property on a magpylib scene object using a dotted path (e.g. 'color', 'magnetization.arrow.width'); for several style edits at once prefer the batch tool. The value is validated by magpylib; on failure the result contains the validation error - correct the path/value and retry. The Studio view refreshes automatically. Path visualization styles (the line/markers drawn along an object's movement path, e.g. a sensor sweep) live under 'path.*': 'path.line.color', 'path.marker.color', 'path.show'. Note: on magnets, magnetization coloring (a blue-white-red gradient) is shown by default and masks the base 'color' - when the user wants a visible solid color, also set 'magnetization.mode' to 'arrow' (or 'magnetization.show' to false).

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

value.description: New value for the property (string, number, boolean, or array as required by the schema).
